narrative.overview: China Travel OS looks like a well-kept traveler's notebook: honest, lived-in, organized with care but never precious. Every visual choice serves one goal — getting the reader to the answer as directly as possible, with warmth that comes from the voice and the details, not from decorative styling. The palette is built around a single committed red, used boldly on the newsletter block and buttons, whisper-quiet everywhere else. Typography pairs a literary serif for headings with a humanist sans for body, creating hierarchy through scale and weight contrast without resorting to all-caps eyebrow labels above every section.
keyCharacteristics: Single committed accent color carrying 30–60% of visible surface
Border-based depth hierarchy — no shadows except on city card hover
Serif headings + sans body with ≥1.25 scale ratio between steps
Flat backgrounds, chroma-neutral off-white, no warm-cream tint
Section labels used exactly once (Anxiety zone), not as site-wide scaffolding
All motion respects prefers-reduced-motion and uses targeted transitions only

rules.name: The No-Pure-Gray Rule
rules.body: Every neutral on the site is tinted toward the brand red hue. If a gray reads as purely achromatic, it's wrong. The shift is barely perceptible (0.002–0.005 chroma) — it should feel natural, not colored.

rules.name: The Committed Red Rule
rules.body: Brand red is not an accent sprinkle; it's a structural color. The newsletter block, primary buttons, links, and logo all use it. Together they occupy 30–60% of the visible surface on any given scroll.

rules.name: The Not-Cream Rule
rules.body: The body background (#FAFAFA) is chroma-zero off-white. It must never drift into warm-neutral territory (cream, sand, parchment, ivory). If it looks like paper aged in a drawer, it's wrong.

rules.name: The One Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: The .section-label (small uppercase tracked label) appears in exactly one place: the Anxiety section on the homepage. Every other section lets its h2 carry meaning without a kicker.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If an element needs depth, use a border or a background-color shift. Never use box-shadow as decoration.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Cards, nav, and sections are separated by 1px solid borders. A 1px border and a soft wide drop shadow on the same element is prohibited. Pick the border.

dos: Use the single brand red (#D94838) for buttons, links, the newsletter block, and the logo accent
Differentiate surfaces with 1px borders (#F2EFED / #E6E0DD), not shadows
Pair Literata headings with Work Sans body text
Use cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0, 1) for all interactive transitions; target specific properties
Use text-wrap: balance on all h1–h3 elements
donts: Don't use Chinese cultural motifs, red lanterns, gold accents, or ornate decoration
Don't use SaaS landing-page clichés: gradient buttons, hero-metric templates, buzzwords
Don't use AI-generated marketing cadences: aphoristic negation, em-dash overuse, identical card grids
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe
Don't add .section-label to any new section beyond the Anxiety zone
Don't use warm-tinted backgrounds (cream, sand, parchment, ivory)
Don't pair 1px border with soft wide drop shadow on the same element
Don't use border-radius larger than 16px on cards or sections
Don't use transition: all — target properties explicitly
Don't use glassmorphism, backdrop-filter blur, or gradient text
